macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks end lower as AI concerns and oil surge weigh
items.summary: The Dow fell 1.18% to 52,241.55, the S&P 500 declined 0.43% to 7,629.92, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.08% to 25,986.95. Concerns about the financing and profitability of heavy artificial-intelligence investment offset relative stability in technology shares.[2]

items.title: Oil rises above $100 as Middle East tensions revive inflation concerns
items.summary: U.S. crude climbed back above $100 a barrel and Brent reached a five-month high as markets worried about supply disruptions. The move increased inflation concerns and added pressure to equities.[1]

items.title: Fed expected to hold rates next week while markets watch December outlook
items.summary: Investors broadly expect the Federal Reserve to leave rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting, while seeking clues about whether a December rate hike remains possible. Markets were also positioned cautiously ahead of the Fed decision and a heavy earnings calendar.[1][4]

items.title: U.S. consumer sentiment weakens as inflation expectations rise
items.summary: The University of Michigan’s October survey showed consumer sentiment near a record low, with higher prices linked to the Middle East conflict worsening household views of the economy. Inflation expectations reached their highest level since May.[2][9]

items.title: U.S. private-sector growth eases in October
items.summary: S&P Global’s flash purchasing-managers data indicated slower private-sector growth, while employment increased and selling prices rose at their fastest pace since August 2022.[9]

items.title: American Express plans workforce reduction after mixed quarter
items.summary: American Express reported third-quarter revenue slightly below Wall Street expectations and disclosed plans to eliminate about 5% of its global workforce.[9]

items.title: SLB beats estimates and raises profit forecast
items.summary: Oilfield-services company SLB exceeded third-quarter profit expectations and raised its profit forecast, sending its shares up 6.7% in Friday trading.[2]

items.title: Western Digital beats quarterly estimates
items.summary: Western Digital reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings of $4.64 per share on $4.38 billion in revenue, exceeding estimates of $4.07 per share and $4.13 billion.[4]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,000 as crypto liquidations reach $1.19 billion
items.summary: Bitcoin rose roughly 0.5% over 24 hours to about $82,000, while the broader market recorded approximately $1.19 billion in liquidations. Ether liquidations were about $356 million, exceeding Bitcoin’s roughly $298 million.[1][2]

items.title: Initia blockchain reportedly exploited for about $2.6 million
items.summary: Initia appears to have suffered an exploit involving unauthorized minting of a large volume of tokens. The attacker reportedly cashed out approximately $2.6 million, with additional funds still moving.[1]

items.title: Ethereum delays Glamsterdam Hoodi testnet upgrade
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade scheduled for the Hoodi testnet on October 26, 2026. A replacement activation date has not yet been announced.[1]

items.title: Thailand prepares Bitcoin and Ether ETF rules
items.summary: Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission completed draft rules allowing cryptocurrency ETFs, initially limited to Bitcoin and Ether, to trade on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. The rules are scheduled to take effect October 16, 2026.[1]

items.title: Spain tightens crypto ATM identity checks
items.summary: Spain approved regulations requiring reliable identity verification for all transactions at crypto ATMs. Operators will receive an 18-month transition period to implement enhanced electronic verification.[1]

items.title: Coinbase Ireland fined €3.25 million by Central Bank
items.summary: The Central Bank of Ireland fined Coinbase Ireland €3.25 million for failures involving customer-fund safeguards and reliance on its U.S. parent for controls.[1]

items.title: Solana begins removing floating-point operations from core protocol
items.summary: Anza said it has started removing floating-point calculations from Solana’s core protocol. The first change, SIMD-0391, activated on mainnet beta epoch 1026 and replaces floating-point logic in stake-program and validator-client warm-up and cool-down processes.[1]

items.title: Aave Pro launches yield-comparison and one-click deposit feature
items.summary: Aave Pro introduced Earn, a feature that lets users compare asset yields and make one-click deposits into selected opportunities.[1]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI makes Decisions API generally available
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly released its Decisions API to all customers, targeting fast, low-cost classification, routing, and other decision tasks in AI applications.

items.title: Google Cloud adds OpenAI models alongside Gemini and Claude
items.summary: Google Cloud reportedly began offering OpenAI models in private preview alongside its own Gemini models and Anthropic’s Claude, expanding multi-model enterprise access on one platform.

items.title: Microsoft reports strong performance from medical AI system
items.summary: Microsoft says its MAI-DxO system substantially outperformed physicians on difficult diagnostic cases, while plans call for further evaluation in a hospital setting.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Kumo Relational foundation model
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly launched Kumo Relational, a predictive analytics foundation model designed to work directly with enterprise data without additional model training.

items.title: IBM open-sources Granite Speech 5.0
items.summary: IBM reportedly released Granite Speech 5.0, a speech-recognition model intended to improve transcription in noisy and reverberant environments.

items.title: Inception Labs releases Mercury 3 diffusion model
items.summary: Inception Labs announced Mercury 3, a diffusion-based AI model that claims competitive performance while running four to eight times faster than comparable systems.

items.title: Hugging Face releases Carbon-X for DNA research
items.summary: Hugging Face reportedly released Carbon-X, an open model that lets researchers interact with DNA sequences using natural-language questions; it is not validated for medical decisions.

items.title: Uber expands ChatGPT Work to 30,000 employees
items.summary: Uber reportedly rolled out OpenAI’s workplace agent to approximately 30,000 employees after an earlier pilot, broadening enterprise use of AI-assisted work tools.

items.title: Warp Sciences raises $215 million for AI-driven drug discovery
items.summary: Warp Sciences, founded by former OpenAI science chief Kevin Weil, reportedly raised $215 million to build increasingly automated chemistry laboratories for drug developers.

items.title: Bolt selects NVIDIA AI for planned Lucid robotaxis
items.summary: Bolt reportedly selected NVIDIA’s Alpamayo driving AI for a planned Lucid robotaxi fleet, with data collection in Madrid expected in 2027 subject to regulatory approval.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches
items.summary: Activision and Infinity Ward released Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on October 23, featuring a campaign, rebuilt DMZ mode and redesigned multiplayer. A launch patch reportedly addresses progression problems and adjusts enemy AI.

items.title: EA reportedly closes BioWare and cuts about 400 jobs
items.summary: Electronic Arts is reportedly shutting BioWare and reducing its global workforce by roughly 400 positions as the publisher shifts toward live-service, competitive and persistent online games.

items.title: Esports Nations Cup postponed to 2027
items.summary: The Esports Foundation has delayed the inaugural Esports Nations Cup in Riyadh from November 2026 to November 2027, affecting players, coaches and federations that had planned around the original schedule.

items.title: Riot extends 2XKO community-event support
items.summary: Riot Games will continue its start.gg Community Events Support programme for 2XKO through the end of 2027, despite plans for active development of the fighting game to end in 2026.

items.title: Riot suspends LFL player during integrity investigation
items.summary: Riot Games provisionally suspended TLN Pirates player Tomislav Nanjara on October 22 while investigating a competitive-integrity matter in France’s League of Legends LFL.

items.title: Creative Assembly investigates generative AI in pulled remaster
items.summary: Creative Assembly said the cancelled SHOGUN 2 remaster was developed outside the studio and that it is investigating how generative AI was used in the project’s assets.

items.title: AION 2 surpasses 400,000 concurrent players
items.summary: NC reported that AION 2 exceeded 400,000 concurrent players within 18 days and accumulated 108.2 million hours played since its global launch.

items.title: Epic launches AI-focused creator game jam
items.summary: Epic Games announced a game jam for Unreal Engine and UEFN creators offering continuation grants of up to $50,000; reports indicate an initial requirement to use AI was later removed.

items.title: US video-game market remains broadly stable
items.summary: Circana data cited by GamesMarket.Global put US video-game spending at $4.76 billion in September, slightly below the prior year, while hardware and accessories returned to year-over-year growth.
